thread:
emily: FYI — were enabling a new GPU class (G6-Max-Q) in AMS (ams-1a / ams-1b) starting 03:00 UTC tonight. This is targeted at dense compute workloads (large batch inferencing). Reservations + a new rotation policy will be in effect. See summary below.

raj: Quick q — is this a replacement for any existing pools or additive?

emily: Additive for now. We'll gradually reallocate some burst capacity from older preemptible pools (A100-preemptible) into G6-Max-Q as commit contracts allow. No forced migrations — you'll keep existing pools unless you opt in.

emily: Key points:
• Regions: ams-1a, ams-1b (initial); parity to other EU zones next quarter.
• Initial capacity: ~48 cards total (expected to expand weekly).
• Reservation type: "rotation" reservations are enabled — they provide time-sliced access so many teams can hold reservations without blocking each other.
• Priority: Enterprise reserved contracts > Dedicated > rotation-reserved > burst.

emily: Reservation CLI example:
```
redwood reserve create --pool g6-max-q --region ams --duration 30d --rotation --cards 4 --name "ml-batch-q"
```
This creates a rotation reservation that gets guaranteed x cards for short windows across the month.

capacity-bot: System update — current available cards in ams-1a: 26, ams-1b: 22. Estimated nightly replenish: +8 cards (03:00 UTC).

tamika: Any billing changes for rotation reservations?

finance-bot: Rotation reservations are billed pro-rata at 60% of a full dedicated card rate (this reflects time-sliced access). Effective tonight for new reservations; existing reserved contracts unchanged. Detailed price table: https://intra.redwood/gpu-pricing#rotation (internal).

michael: Console note — we need a UI hint explaining rotation windows and the billing model. Putting a small tooltip + link on the reservation flow. Planning a deploy tomorrow morning.

sara: For teams doing latency-sensitive online models: do not use rotation reservations for production-critical endpoints. Recommend dedicated or pinned pools. We'll add a nudge in the console flow.

jake: Are there performance differences vs. A100 for FP16 and int8?

emily: Slightly different perf curve — G6-Max-Q is optimized for dense batch throughput and lower mem per card. For fp16 throughput expect similar or better in batch scenarios; int8 quantization paths are supported but profiling recommended. Well publish microbenchmarks in docs.

oncall-sre: Heads-up — a short maintenance window in ams-1b tonight 02:40-03:10 UTC to move hosts. Rotation reservations will be paused during that window. If you have critical runs, schedule outside that time.

raj: If a team wants migration help from A100 pools -> G6-Max-Q, who do we ping?

emily: Ping #eng-ml and include sample traces + perf targets. Well run a mapping review and, if needed, create an automated recommend job that suggests config changes and quantization profiles.

jake: Any limits on # of rotation reservations per org?

emily: Soft limit 5 active rotation reservations per org by default; you can request more via the quota form — approvals done by capacity team.

capacity-bot: Note: To opt into nightly expansion list, run: `redwood capacity opt-in --region ams --pool g6-max-q`

tamika: Sounds good. Will tell infra teams about the billing note.

michael: I'll schedule the console tooltip deploy and update the release notes.

emily: TL;DR: G6-Max-Q live in AMS tonight, rotation reservations enabled, billing = 60% proration, maintenance window affects short period. Please test with non-critical batches first and ping #eng-ml for migration help. :thumbsup:

sara: Thanks!

oncall-sre: Incident note — if you see reservation failures during 02:40-03:10 UTC file an incident and tag oncall. Well post a follow-up summary after the maintenance.

emily: Will follow up with a short playbook and the bench markdown tomorrow.
